Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 94, verse 1–8:

(p-296) Surah al-Sharh

Meccan by consensus.

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Did We not expand your breast for you?﴾ This is a statement from God, may He be exalted, to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) regarding the expansion of his breast for what He had laden him with of prophethood.

Regarding "nashrah" (We expand) there are two interpretations:

The first: that is, We removed your concern from you, so that you may be free for what you have been commanded to do.

The second: that is, We open your breast so that it may be wide enough for what you have borne, so that it does not become constricted. From this comes "tashrih al-lahm" (slicing meat), because one opens it in order to dry it into jerky.

Regarding that by which his breast was expanded, there are three sayings. The first: Islam; this is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second: that it was filled with wisdom and knowledge; this is the view of al-Hasan.

The third: by what He bestowed upon him of patience and forbearance; this is the view of ʿAta'.

It may also admit a fourth: by the preservation of the Qur'an and the rights of prophethood.

﴿And We removed from you your burden﴾ Regarding this there are three sayings: (p-297)

The first: "and We forgave you your sin"; this is the view of Mujahid. Qatadah said: the Prophet had sins that weighed heavily upon him, and God, may He be exalted, forgave them for him.

The second: "and We lightened from you your load"; this is the view of al-Suddi.

It is in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "and We loosened from you your burden" (wiqrak).

The third: "and We protected you before prophethood, during the forty years, from defilements, until revelation descended upon you while you were purified from defilements."

It may also admit a fourth: that is, We removed from you the obligation of what you could not bear. For the prophets, although they bore the weights of prophethood to a degree that others of the community would be unable to bear, were given of the abundance of strength by which they could bear the weight of prophethood; thus what others were unable to bear became, for them, not beyond their capacity.

﴿Which weighed down your back﴾ That is, it made your back heavy; this is said by Ibn Zayd, like a camel that buckles under a heavy load until it becomes "naqd" (broken-backed).

Regarding this there are three aspects:

The first: it made his back heavy with sins until He forgave them.

The second: it made his back heavy with the message until he conveyed it.

The third: it made his back heavy with blessings until he gave thanks for them.

﴿And We raised high your remembrance﴾ Regarding this there are three sayings: The first: "and We raised high your remembrance through prophethood"; this is the view of Yahya ibn Salam.

The second: "and We raised high your remembrance in the Hereafter as We raised it in this world."

The third: that you are mentioned along with me whenever I am mentioned. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Jibril (peace be upon him) came to me and said: Indeed God, may He be exalted, says: Do you know how I have raised your remembrance? He said: God knows best. He said: Whenever I am mentioned, you are mentioned." Qatadah said: God raised his remembrance in this world and the Hereafter, so there is no preacher who delivers a sermon or recites the tashahhud, nor any person of prayer, except that he proclaims: I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God.

﴿Indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾ Regarding this there are two aspects: (p-298)

The first: indeed, with striving for this world comes the good of the Hereafter.

The second: indeed, with hardship comes ease, with patience comes abundance, with wretchedness comes happiness, and with roughness comes smoothness.

It may admit three aspects:

The first: indeed, with hardship there is ease with God, so that He may do with either of them as He wills.

The second: indeed, with hardship in this world there is ease in the Hereafter.

The third: indeed, with hardship for one who is tested there is ease for one who is patient and seeks reward, through what he is granted of contentment, or through what he is given of abundance.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, if hardship were in a hole, ease would seek it out until it entered upon it. (And hardship will never overcome two eases)." The word "hardship" (al-ʿusr) is singular in both places and "ease" (al-yusr) is dual, because the definite article is attached to "ʿusr" and omitted from "yusr."

Regarding the repetition of ﴿with hardship comes ease﴾ there are two aspects:

The first: what we have mentioned, the singularity of hardship and the duality of ease, so that it may be stronger for hope and more encouraging to patience; this is the view of Tha'lab.

The second: for emphasis and intensification, as they say in repeating a reply, "Yes, yes" and "No, no." This is the view of al-Farra'. And a poet said:

"I resolved to put myself beyond some of the cares, so woe to myself, woe to it."

﴿So when you are free, then strive﴾ Regarding this there are four interpretations: The first: so when you are free from the obligatory duties, then strive in the night prayer; this is the view of Ibn Mas'ud.

The second: so when you are free from your prayer, then strive in your supplication; this is the view of al-Dahhak. (p-299)

The third: so when you are free from your jihad against your enemy, then strive in the worship of your Lord; this is the view of al-Hasan and Qatadah.

The fourth: so when you are free from the affairs of your worldly life, then strive in the work of your Hereafter; this is the view of Mujahid.

It may admit a fifth interpretation: so when you are free from conveying the message, then strive in jihad against your enemy.

﴿And to your Lord turn with desire﴾ Regarding this there are three aspects:

The first: turn toward Him with desire in your supplication; this is the view of Ibn Mas'ud.

The second: in your assistance.

The third: in the sincerity of your intention; this is the view of Mujahid.

It may admit a fourth: turn toward Him with desire for your victory over your enemies.

(p-296) Surah al-Sharh

Meccan by consensus.

The first: that is, We removed your concern from you, so that you may be free for what you have been commanded to do.

The second: that is, We open your breast so that it may be wide enough for what you have borne, so that it does not become constricted. From this comes "tashrih al-lahm" (slicing meat), because one opens it in order to dry it into jerky.

The second: that it was filled with wisdom and knowledge; this is the view of al-Hasan.

The first: "and We forgave you your sin"; this is the view of Mujahid. Qatadah said: the Prophet had sins that weighed heavily upon him, and God, may He be exalted, forgave them for him.

The second: "and We lightened from you your load"; this is the view of al-Suddi.

The third: "and We protected you before prophethood, during the forty years, from defilements, until revelation descended upon you while you were purified from defilements."

The second: it made his back heavy with the message until he conveyed it.

The third: it made his back heavy with blessings until he gave thanks for them.
